cost: The original borrow rejection delayed qualification of four real-source admission controls. The missing execution scope can delay an operand temporary's destructor until after a later operand has run. The first executable qualification ran zero tests and supplied no old-versus-new Drop-order verdict. The second fixture attempt linked an unnecessary std panic/backtrace path and again supplied no old/new executable verdict.
cause: Lazy Boolean operands are lowered without their own temporary-scope boundaries. The shared borrow carried by committed_packs(...).unwrap().is_some() is kept drop-live until the surrounding if ends, across the following mutable lease call. The existing two-phase activation check correctly rejects that overlong lowered lifetime. Separately, the initial executable oracle used mutable globals, whose StaticMut flow form the strict source test gate cannot verify. The real-core native wrapper also left its library and panic contract implicit: omitting no_std linked std and its backtrace path into a freestanding C-entry oracle.
whys: Blaze rejected the shared lookup followed by a mutable operation in a short-circuit condition.
The Option containing an opaque iterator was still drop-live when the later mutable receiver activated.
Borrow-flow lowering cleaned the temporary only after the entire if condition, rather than after its Boolean operand.
The lazy-Boolean paths in borrow-flow and executable lowering omitted operand-local temporary scopes; flattened let chains also need to distinguish ordinary Boolean links from pattern scrutinees.

Existing condition and borrow controls did not require an owned reference-carrying operand temporary to finish before a sibling operand, with observable destructor order and a genuinely live-borrow negative.
The initial executable oracle's mutable global counters were not eligible for strict source verification, so an observer failure could not be classified as the intended semantic assertion failure.

Changing the native guest from no_core to the installed core did not explicitly declare no_std and a bounded panic handler, so the fixture depended on unrelated std backtrace resolution before its oracle could execute.
class: lowered control flow omits language-defined temporary lifetime boundaries
prevention: Give ordinary lazy operands explicit scopes in both lowerings, keep Boolean destinations alive outside those scopes, and preserve let-chain scrutinees and bindings. Add causal borrow-acceptance and actual destructor-order controls plus a live-borrow rejection; retain the unchanged distributed helper as full source acceptance. The executable oracle must use checked state and retain BLAZE_TESTS=verify, exactly-one-executed-test receipts, and a specific old semantic failure. The Rust Reference specifies each lazy Boolean operand as a temporary scope: https://doc.rust-lang.org/reference/destructors.html#temporary-scopes. The native oracle declares its real-core-only link closure and nonreturning panic contract; a deliberate checked overflow under that exact wrapper must reach the named abort trap, not return zero, fail frontend checking, or hang.
fix: Borrow-flow BranchOperand preserves the Boolean outside each operand's temporary scope, closes the scope, then branches. Structural traversal stays linear. Executable lowering uses the existing open/close machinery for both lazy operands and ordinary Boolean links in let chains; pattern scrutinees retain their condition/body scope. The existing temporary-lifetime integration target contains six valid cases and three genuinely live E0502 controls with completed borrow checking. Its shared executable oracle now uses stack-owned core::cell::Cell counters borrowed by Probe, preserves all thirteen expected creation/destruction checks, and uses the real installed core in the native wrapper as well. The distributed helper, loan/conflict rules, strict test gate and acceptance receipts remain unchanged. After an independent rule-66 review, the native guest boundary is rebuilt with no_std, no_main, and a standard panic_handler calling real core::intrinsics::abort_immediate. The same existing test runs the unchanged positive oracle and an alternate ordinary u8 addition of 255 and 1 under the exact same MAIN and NewFront. The negative arm accepts only RunError::Trapped with TrapCode::Lir equal to ABORT_TRAP (0xfe00). The real shelf, OverflowChecks::On, four test names and all source receipts remain unchanged; no new runtime stub or std resolver change is introduced.
